label: StudySS2 device-confidence re-record (logprobs ON) and RefSpatial rescore: controls and provenance
user_ruling: 2026-11-20: re-record the StudySS2 single-shot DEVICE answers with logprobs on so the five cascade arms get a real answer-confidence instead of None, and rescore RefSpatial with the fixed point parser. Greedy decoding unchanged, so the answers must reproduce the committed run and that equality is the control.

server_config.stack: Jetson AGX Orin, vLLM 0.20.0, orin3_serve.sh verbatim: released image processor, NO --mm-processor-kwargs, --limit-mm-per-prompt image:9, --enforce-eager, --max-num-seqs 1, --enable-prefix-caching, --max-model-len 32768, --seed 0.
server_config.source_of_truth: refspatial_compare.json ttft_condition.device_stack ('vLLM 0.20.0+cu126, released image processor, no --mm-processor-kwargs'). This is NOT the ACC2/ORIN-REC server (which forces shortest_edge 4096, cap 640); the SS2 device stack uses released mm defaults.
server_config.only_addition: FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 env (cubin version-mismatch safety, inert to the model/image-processor config, so it cannot affect the answer-equality control).
server_config.cached_tokens: vLLM 0.20.0 does not populate cached_tokens on the device; absent throughout (as refspatial_compare.json records).
server_config.sizing_param_note: The committed StudySS2 row records max_model_len 8192 and gpu_mem_util 0.22; this run used orin3_serve.sh defaults max_model_len 32768 and gpu_mem_util 0.4. These are KV-cache sizing parameters only: every SS2 prompt is <=1797 tokens (fits both) and neither changes per-prompt logits. The answer-equality control (99.81% exact, below) empirically confirms the configs are equivalent for these items; the image-processor config (released defaults, no mm-kwargs, FLASH_ATTN), which governs visual-token identity, is matched exactly.

producer_change.change: Added a --logprobs flag that wires the pre-existing call(logprobs=...) path into main() and stores the per-token top-20 as rows[].logprobs. The kit (commit 5337d50) shipped the call() plumbing and the downstream consumers (ss2_device_confidence.py expects *_device_logprobs.json) but not the producer wiring; this completes it. Default (no --logprobs) output is byte-unchanged, so the committed path is untouched. Implementation fix, reported here.

staging_control.rule: ss2_build_manifests.py re-extracts images from the re-staged parquet and regenerates the manifests; the regenerated refspatial_manifest.jsonl, realworldqa_manifest.jsonl, ss2_manifest_meta.json and both smoke sets are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed ones (git diff empty).
staging_control.result: PASS. Byte-identity reproduces every image_sha16, qid and ordering from the parquet source. (On-disk PNG sha differs from image_sha16 by construction: image_sha16 is the sha of the raw parquet bytes, the PNG is a PIL re-encode; the answer-equality control is the guard on pixel identity.)

smoke: 5-request realworldqa logprobs smoke: 5/5 scored, 0 errors, per-token top-20 logprobs populated on every row, both mcq and free_form subsets exercised, and all 5 answers matched the committed run.

equality_control.exact: 1040 of 1042 re-recorded answers are byte-identical to committed (realworldqa 764/765, refspatial 276/277).

diffs.diagnosis: a ~50/50 MCQ near-tie; the committed run and my own 5-request smoke both emitted A, the full run emitted C. Same input, two answers: prefix-cache cold/warm numerical nondeterminism (the grey-control / D81 one-logprob-quantum tip). Here the flip happened to land on the CORRECT letter (em 0 -> 1).
one coordinate digit differs by 5 px; SCORE UNCHANGED (point_accuracy 1.0 both, both points inside the GT mask). A single-token near-tie, score-invariant.

equality_control.classification: Both diffs are diagnosed to the deployment's declared prefix-caching cold/warm numerical nondeterminism, not a server-config or method error: 99.81% exact reproduction, one diff score-invariant and one a 0.25-nat MCQ near-tie. Caching is a declared methodological parameter of this run.

Per the proof's own note (lines 112-115), of the 377 recall decisions only 20 are robot questions (which carry a committed answer probability); the other 357 are SINGLE-SHOT, which previously had no answer probability at all.
wiring_proof.what_this_step_changed: This re-record PRODUCES the single-shot answer probabilities that were missing (ss2_device_confidence.json, 1042 questions). It does NOT by itself move the 20/377 line, because device_conf_wiring_proof reads q.device_answer_confidence off the harness query objects and the harness is NOT yet wired to inject ss2_device_confidence.json into the 357 single-shot recall queries.

Per CLAUDE.md it must be flagged and discussed before applying; it was NOT applied overnight. Once wired, re-running this proof should lift the 357 single-shot queries from absent to present.
